\documentclass[11pt]{article}\usepackage[margin=1in]{geometry}\usepackage{amsmath,amssymb,amsthm}\newtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}\newtheorem{remark}{Remark}
\title{Periodic Center-Flux Carriers on the $2^4$ Cubical Torus}\author{}\date{21 July 2026}\begin{document}\maketitle
\begin{abstract}We replace the topology-free open block by an exact periodic $GF(2)$ cochain carrier and construct the six independent center two-flux labels required by a sector-aware retained state.\end{abstract}
Let $C^k$ be periodic cubical cochains on $(\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z)^4$ with $GF(2)$ coefficients. The executable matrices include all coboundaries $d_0,d_1,d_2,d_3$.
\begin{theorem}The cell counts are $(16,64,96,64,16)$, the coboundary ranks are $(15,45,45,15)$, and
\[d_{k+1}d_k=0,\qquad (b_0,b_1,b_2,b_3,b_4)=(1,4,6,4,1).
\]
Six explicit cut-sheet two-cocycles are independent modulo $\operatorname{im}d_1$ and therefore label $2^6=64$ center-flux sectors.\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}Gaussian elimination over $GF(2)$ gives the ranks. Rank-nullity gives the Betti numbers. Appending the six representatives to $d_1$ raises its rank from 45 to 51, while multiplication by $d_2$ vanishes.\end{proof}
These labels can be retained through a periodic block exposure and prevent silent identification of distinct center sectors.
\begin{remark}The construction represents $GF(2)$ center two-flux, not the integer second Chern class or instanton number of a smooth $SU(2)$ bundle. It is a topology carrier, not complete topological control.\end{remark}\end{document}
